name: AppNav
intent: The app's main navigation: a brand rail of sections on the left, each with an optional second-level menu that flies out beside it.
usage: Put one AppNav on the left of the app shell, under the AppHeader, full height. It is one component: items are the rail sections (icon and label), endItems sit at the bottom of the rail, and a section's children make its second-level menu. Hovering a section rolls its menu out beside the rail; moving off the nav or picking a link rolls it back in. The menu's header row, which holds the section name and the pin, is 48px like a rail row, over 40px link rows. Every menu is the same width, the longest link in the whole nav (within --side-nav-panel-min and --side-nav-panel-max), so the menu never resizes as people move from one section to another, whether the rail is expanded or not. Clicking a section opens its first link, so a section with no menu still works. pin docks the menu open beside the rail; the × closes it. expanded shows the labels (the AppHeader menu button toggles it). A menu can name its folders: a child can be a group, { label, items }, which draws a 12px header row on the rule above its links. When the menu is pinned the header also carries an expand/collapse control at the far right, in the pin's column; in a flyout it is the rule and the label alone and nothing collapses. Groups start open and a collapse lasts only while the menu is out. A long menu is kept on screen and scrolls with overflow rows at the top and bottom. loading is the boot state: an icon block and a label bar on each row while the nav is still arriving. See contracts/appnav.json for the full contract. In a box narrower than 640px, the kit's mobile break, there is no room for a rail beside the page, so the nav is a drawer: it takes its open width with the labels shown whether or not expanded is passed, and it leaves the sliding to the frame around it.

items.itemShape: { id: string; label: string; icon: string; href?: string; children?: AppNavChild[] } | { divider: true }
items.note: Rail sections, top to bottom. In the app shell this is always the full app nav, APP_NAV from @/patterns/AppShell/appNav (with APP_NAV_END as endItems); never a shorter or made-up list. icon is a Material Symbols name. children is the second-level menu, made of { id, label, href? } links, { label, items } groups (a named folder of links) and { divider: true } lines. A menu can mix all three. A group holds links only: no group inside a group.

endItems.note: Sections pinned to the bottom of the rail, like Recycle Bin and Processes. Same shape as items.

current.note: Controlled id of the current page: a section or a link in its menu. Marks the link and its section.

defaultCurrent.note: Starting page when current is not controlled; AppNav then moves it on each click.

onNavigate.note: (id: string) => void. A section click passes its first link's id (or its own id when it has no menu).

expanded.note: Rail shows labels, 170px wide. Off, it is a 56px icon rail. Wire it to the AppHeader navOpen. Expanded, the row's cascade chevron goes: the section row itself carries aria-expanded and opens the menu on Enter.

pinned.note: Controlled pin. The menu docks beside the rail, full height, with a border and no shadow, and pushes the page over.

defaultPinned.note: Starting pin when pinned is not controlled. The docked menu is the current section's, or the first section with a menu until one is opened.

onPinnedChange.note: (pinned: boolean) => void. Called by the pin and × buttons in the menu header.

loading.note: Booting: the rail keeps its brand fill and its 48px rows, with a brand-tone icon block and, when it is open, a label bar for each section it was given. AppShell hands this down when the frame is loading, so a screen sets nothing.

useWhen: The main navigation of the app shell, on every page.
Sections with their own pages under them: the rail picks the section, the menu picks the page.
A section with enough pages to name folders inside its menu: give each run of links a group.
doNot: Do not invent a Sidebar, NavRail, Flyout or local menu beside it.
Do not put page actions, filters or tabs in it. Those belong in the page.
Do not nest a third level. A section has one menu of links, split by dividers.
Do not use Dropdown or Tabs for app navigation.
Do not expect the group collapse control in a flyout. It is pinned-only; a hovered menu shows the rule and the label and nothing collapses.
Do not indent a group's links. They keep the same 16px inset as every other link, so the menu stays narrow.
Do not uppercase a group label or darken it. It is written as authored, 12px semibold in the subtle text color, so it stays quieter than the links.
Do not nest a group inside a group, or put a section's own links under a group of the same name.
a11y: A nav landmark named by label. Sections and links are real links (or buttons without href) you Tab through.
Enter on a section opens its page. The chevron after a section with a menu is its cascade button: Enter opens the menu and moves focus into it, with aria-expanded.
Tab moves through the menu links. Escape leaves the menu back to its cascade button; Escape in the rail closes an open menu.
The current page has aria-current=page. On touch, a tap on a section with a menu opens the menu.
Collapsed rail icons show their label in a kit Tooltip. The roll animation turns off with reduced motion.
A group label names its own list of links (aria-labelledby), so the links are announced as belonging to it.
Pinned, the group's control is a real button named by the group label, with aria-expanded and aria-controls on the group's list. In a flyout the label is plain text and there is no button.
Expanded, the rail has no cascade button: the section row carries aria-expanded and aria-controls, and Enter on it opens the menu and moves focus into it instead of following the link.
snippet:
<AppNav
  items={sections}
  endItems={[{ id: "recycle", label: "Recycle Bin", icon: "recycling" }]}
  current={pageId}
  onNavigate={openPage}
  expanded={navOpen}
/>

examples.title: Rail
examples.usage: The closed rail: icons only. Hover Revenue or Settings for their menu; click a section to open its first page.

examples.title: Expanded
examples.usage: expanded shows the labels and drops the cascade chevron; Enter on a section opens its menu. Hover AR for a flyout: its groups show the rule and the label, with nothing to collapse.

examples.title: Pinned
examples.usage: The menu docked open beside the rail, with a border and no shadow. × closes it. Here General Ledger is the current page, so Revenue and its link show selected.

examples.title: Groups
examples.usage: AR's menu pinned open: Ledgers, Payments, Lockbox and Credits head their links on the rule above them. Pinned, each header carries a chevron at the far right that collapses its links; the links keep the same inset as every other link.

examples.title: Booting
examples.usage: The rail while the nav is still arriving: one row of blocks per section.
